hook: A skier fell 60 feet into a glacier crevasse
narration: A skier fell sixty feet into a crevasse on Mount Baker.
A Navy helicopter crew from Whidbey Island flew up to find him.
He was a thousand feet higher on the mountain than first reported.
Crew members were lowered onto the glacier with a litter.
Helicopters avoid landing on glaciers, where snow can hide more crevasses, so crews hoist instead.
The corpsman checked him, and they hoisted him up in the litter.
outcome: The crew flew him to a hospital in Bellingham.
preview_ok: Checked by eye: the glacier shots (30 to 33, 36 to 39, 81 to 84 s) show the rescuers and the dark crevasse opening on white snow; EMPTY misfires on the uniform snowfield.
title: Skier fell 60 feet into a crevasse
description:
A Navy search and rescue crew from Naval Air Station Whidbey Island hoisted a skier who fell into a 60 foot crevasse on Mount Baker, Washington, June 4, 2017, and flew him to a hospital in Bellingham.

Footage: U.S. Navy video, Naval Air Station Whidbey Island Search and Rescue, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/529650/nas-whidbey-island-sar-rescues-olympic-mountains-and-mt-baker
